title: Off-center sum as a weighted sum
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $x$ be a sign vector of length $n$, and let $f$ map sign vectors of length $n$ to signs. The sum over all sign vectors $a\ne x$ of the prescribed Fourier kernel at $(a,x)$ multiplied by the real value of $f(a)$ equals the sum over all sign vectors $a$ of the same product, with the kernel factor set to zero when $a=x$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of the $n$ coordinates
$x$ is a sign vector of length $n$
$f$ maps sign vectors of length $n$ to signs
